description: The Shannon entropy of a Collatz trajectory's odd/even step sequence encodes structural information about the starting number. Numbers with high delay have step sequences with entropy approaching the theoretical maximum of H = -p*log(p) - (1-p)*log(1-p) where p = ln(2)/ln(3). This information-theoretic lens reveals why some numbers resist convergence.
mathematical_formalization: Let sigma(n) = (s_1, s_2, ..., s_{D(n)}) be the parity sequence where s_i = 1 if T^i(n) is odd, 0 if even. Define H(n) = -sum_{i=1}^{D(n)} [s_i * log(s_i/O(n)) + (1-s_i) * log((1-s_i)/E(n))]. High-delay numbers maximize H(n) while maintaining C(n) = O(n)/E(n) near ln(2)/ln(3) ~ 0.6309.
analogical_connections: Like maximum entropy distributions in statistical mechanics - delay records are 'maximum entropy' trajectories
Analogous to channel capacity in communication theory - the Collatz channel has a capacity determined by log2(3)
Similar to how DNA sequences with high Shannon entropy encode more functional information
implementation_hypothesis: For each candidate, compute the running Shannon entropy of the parity sequence during iteration. If entropy drops below threshold early, abort the computation (the trajectory will converge quickly).
experiment_seed: Compute Shannon entropy of parity sequences for the known 147 delay records. Plot H(n) vs D(n) and fit a regression. Use the fit to predict the entropy of the next undiscovered delay record.
